heading: INT. PIANO TUNER'S WORKSHOP - EARLY MORNING

units.text: INT. PIANO TUNER'S WORKSHOP - EARLY MORNING
A narrow workshop of felt, wire, and old oak.
Hammers hang in rows like tiny skulls.
A gutted upright piano stands against one wall, its keys exposed.
Gray light through a dusty skylight.
MARGUERITE OYELOWO-STRAND, 60s, small and exact, in a canvas apron, sits at a bench with a tuning lever in her hand.
Her hair is pinned up with a pencil.
Her glasses are pushed onto her forehead.
She presses a single key, and a note hangs in the air, flat.
An answering machine on the shelf blinks red.
She regards it.
She reaches over and presses PLAY.
You've reached Oyelowo-Strand Piano Service. Leave a message and I'll return your call.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: BEEP.
Silence on the tape.
Nine seconds of breath, nothing more.
Then a click.
She rewinds.
Plays it again.
The same nine seconds of breath.
She sets down the lever.
Her thumb moves back and forth across the rim of the bench, back and forth.
She presses the key again.
The note is still flat.
She picks up the lever, fits it to the pin, and gives a quarter turn.
Another press.
The note rises.
It is nearly right.
She plays the nine seconds one more time.
Midway, her hand closes on the lever hard enough to whiten the knuckles.
The tape clicks off.
The lever snaps against the piano's iron frame, a harsh sharp CLANG that rings through the workshop.
She stands.
Walks to the machine.
Pulls the plug from the wall.
The red light dies.
Then she sits at the keys and plays a single slow chord, four notes, perfectly in tune.
She holds it until the sound is gone.
